newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Holocaust siren brings Israel to a halt.
newsitem.headline: Holocaust siren brings Israel to a halt.

text.p: The wail of a memorial siren brought Israel to a standstill for two minutes on the Jewish state's annual remembrance day on Monday for the six million Jews killed in the Nazi Holocaust.

Traffic stopped and motorists stood by their cars as the air raid siren sounded. Flags throughout Israel were at half-mast for the 24-hour memorial and Israeli television showed footage from Nazi death camps where Jews were exterminated.
Israeli leaders, the country's chief rabbis and public officials went to parliament to read aloud the names of relatives, many of them children, who perished in the Holocaust.
"Every person has a name and every survivor has testimony," Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in the Knesset, reading a list of his wife Sara's relatives killed by the Nazis.
He said more than 100 members of his wife's family died in Europe and only her father, who came to Palestine as a youth before World War II, and two other relatives survived.
Adolf Hitler began persecuting Jews after seizing power in Germany in 1933. The slaughter of Jews known as the Nazis' "Final Solution" began in the early years of World War II.

A Jerusalem symposium on the battle to reclaim Jewish assets looted during the war -- efforts now focused on Switzerland's wartime economic links with the Third Reich -- showed that much of the Holocaust's history had yet to be exposed.

"The entire continent of Europe was afflicted," Jewish Agency chairman Avraham Burg told the symposium attended by Jean-Francois Bergier, head of an independent panel formed by Switzerland to probe allegations it hoarded Holocaust victims' wealth and profited from its wartime dealings.
"There is no country which does not bear the economic imprint of the Jews of Europe before and during the Holocaust," Burg said.

Bergier pledged the historians panel, created in December amid growing criticism of Swiss banks' handling of dormant Holocaust-era accounts and the country's purchases of looted gold from Nazi Germany, would methodically uncover neutral Switzerland's wartime behavior.
"It became clear that the roots of this people were not as clear as it once seemed," Bergier said.
Switzerland this year promised to set up funds to aid Holocaust survivors, months after the outgoing Swiss president likened Jewish calls for restitution to "extortion and blackmail".
Burg praised Switzerland's efforts to confront its history but insisted other European states own up to their wartime records.

"Switzerland is a model. After it will come France. Then Poland. Then all the states where Jews went to the crematorium and did not return and their property became part of the economic infrastructure of other nations," Burg said.
At a memorial ceremony in Jerusalem on Sunday night, Netanyahu said: "Never again will Jewish children be helpless." Some 1.5 million Jewish children were killed by the Nazis.
"Today we vow that we will maintain a strong Israel, that we shall achieve peace for our people and that we shall give our children and grandchildren security and hope," he said.
Netanyahu plunged the Middle East peace process into crisis last month when he gave a green light to bulldozers to break ground for a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Israeli President Ezer Weizman was to meet Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in Gaza on Tuesday to try to revive peace talks. U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross was due in Israel on Wednesday in a new effort to restart the negotiations.
